newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analyst forecasts 4.0 pct rise in EU grain sowings.
newsitem.headline: Analyst forecasts 4.0 pct rise in EU grain sowings.

text.p: French grain analyst Strategie Grains forecast on Wednesday an increase of four percent in European Union grain sowings for the next harvest to 38.2 million hectares.

In its first estimate for the new 1997/98 season, Strategie Grains also predicted that grain production within the European Union might rise by one percent to 206.7 million tonnes from an estimated 203.7 million tonnes produced in 1996/97.

Strategie Grains cautioned that these estimates were "extremely provisional" as farmers had not yet sown spring crops and only four EU member countries had released statistics on winter grain sowings.
Strategie Grains said it assumed that grain yields would drop two percent to 5.4 tonnes per hectare from 5.5 tonnes in 1996/97.
The yield forecast was based on a long-term trend and weather conditions would determine how yields would turn out.

Strategie Grains put 1997/98 soft wheat output at 92.8 million tonnes against an estimated 90.5 million tonnes in 1996/97. This assumed wheat sowings would rise three percent to 14.2 million hectares and yields decline one percent to 6.5 tonnes per hectare.
The analyst also targeted 1997/98 barley production of 52.3 million tonnes against an estimated 52.7 million the previous season.
This assumed barley sowings would rise by four percent to 11.9 million hectares but yields decline by four percent to 4.4 tonnes per hectare.
Strategie Grains expected the European Union to produce 35.5 million tonnes of maize in 1997/98 against 34.1 million tonnes in the previous campaign.
Maize sowings would rise five percent to 4.4 million hectares and yields decline one percent to 8.1 tonnes per hectare.
